findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the `_sanitize_description` / `adf.py` tension: clarify whether `jira_fields.py` moves to `jira_family/` as a whole or only named symbols (`_sanitize_label`, `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`) move while ADF-coupled sanitizers (`_sanitize_description`) stay under `adapters/jira/` — and specify how `jira_family/` provides a description-sanitizer contract that DC can implement with wiki-markup limits instead of ADF limits.
evidence: Plan states: 'jira_fields.py (movable, so it relocates)' in the value-maps resolution paragraph
Plan also states: 'jira_family/ may import neither of them [jira/ nor jira_datacenter/]'
jira_fields.py line 18-20: `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.adf import fit_text_to_adf_limit as _fit_description_to_adf_limit`
`_sanitize_description` in jira_fields.py calls `_fit_description_to_adf_limit` — a symbol from the location-pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`
If jira_fields.py relocates to jira_family/, this import path `from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.adf import ...` would violate the import contract the plan establishes
findings.finding: `jira_fields.py` is described as movable to `jira_family/` wholesale ("jira_fields.py (movable, so it relocates)"), but `jira_fields.py` currently contains `_sanitize_description`, which imports `_fit_description_to_adf_limit` from the location-pinned `adapters/jira/adf.py`. If the whole file moves to `jira_family/`, this import violates the plan's own stated import contract ("jira_family/ may import neither [jira/ nor jira_datacenter/]"), producing a broken import graph. The plan only names `_sanitize_label` and `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK` as moving in the symbol list, but says `jira_fields.py` itself "relocates" — these two claims are in conflict, and neither resolves what happens to `_sanitize_description` and its ADF dependency.
findings.location: Approach §2, sub-bullet: 'Movable to jira_family/ in this epic: _sanitize_label and _RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK' vs. 'jira_fields.py (movable, so it relocates)'
scenarios: Implementer moves jira_fields.py to jira_family/ wholesale; the import-linter contract then fails CI on `jira_family/` importing `adapters/jira/adf`

Implementer splits jira_fields.py, moving only some symbols — but the plan does not state this split or where `_sanitize_description` and `_sanitize_comment` (which also imports from adf via comment_limits) land
DC adapter receives a wrong sanitize_description (ADF-fitted) for wiki-markup bodies, producing a correctness bug
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the `jira_family/` relocation to the ADF-independent symbols only: `_sanitize_label`, `_RELATION_TO_JIRA_LINK`, `_sanitize_summary`, `_sanitize_comment` (comment_limits is already location-pinned by ADR 0035 but the import there goes through `adapters/jira/` directly), and the value maps. Keep `_sanitize_description` under `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` (or make it a method on the `RichTextCodec` contract so each codec can enforce its own length limit without importing `adf.py`).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] J2's AC is amended to resolve the contradiction: either (a) 'acli*.py imports are updated to the new jira_family/ path in this same change' (removing the byte-identical requirement for acli*.py), or (b) the maps stay in adapters/jira/jira_fields.py and acli*.py's reads are excluded from the unification scope.
evidence: J2 de-duplication: '_LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA / _LOCAL_PRIORITY_TO_JIRA — read only by the ACLI transport (acli.py:69-70,143,171; acli_cli_ops.py:34,343,354).'

J2 Approach: 'Per ADR 0035 decision 4, no re-export shims are left at the old paths.'
J2 Approach: 'Every importer and every mock.patch string is updated in this same change.'
findings.finding: J2 contains a direct internal contradiction: it asserts that acli*.py 'are byte-identical to their pre-change state' AND that jira_fields.py (which acli.py:69-70,143,171 and acli_cli_ops.py:34,343,354 directly import) is moved to adapters/jira_family/. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify whether `classify_probe_response` in `jira_family/` will accept `resolved_status_names` as a parameter (or be a method on a configurable object) so DC backends with non-standard workflow names can override the resolved-state set, or explicitly state that the standard `{Resolved, Done, Cancelled}` set is an acceptable shared assumption for both Cloud and DC.
evidence: probe.py line 28: `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})`
probe.py line 33: URL pattern `{jira_url.rstrip('/')}/rest/api/2/issue/{issue_key}?fields=status,resolution` — same REST v2 endpoint DC uses
Plan says DC uses 'REST v2 with wiki-markup/plain-text bodies' but doesn't confirm the probe endpoint is identical
Plan names `classify_probe_response` as moving to `jira_family/` with no mention of parameterizing the resolved-status name set
findings.finding: The plan states `classify_probe_response` moves from `adapters/jira/probe.py` to `jira_family/` and is shared by both Cloud and DC backends. However, `classify_probe_response` currently uses a hardcoded `RESOLVED_STATUS_NAMES = frozenset({"Resolved", "Done", "Cancelled"})` defined in `probe.py`. DC workflow state names may diverge from Cloud (DC installations frequently have custom workflows), yet the plan introduces no parameterization or override for this set in the shared `jira_family/` classifier. The plan also does not address whether DC's probe hits the same REST v2 endpoint shape (`/rest/api/2/issue/{key}?fields=status,resolution`) as the existing Cloud probe (which uses `rest/api/2` today despite Cloud also supporting v3).
findings.location: Approach §2, 'Movable to jira_family/ in this epic: ... classify_probe_response (adapters/jira/probe.py, not location-pinned)'
scenarios: A DC installation uses 'Closed' instead of 'Done' as its resolved state; `classify_probe_response` returns PRESENT_FILTERED instead of PRESENT_RESOLVED, causing the reconciler to perpetually re-fetch issues that are actually resolved
The shared classifier is correct for standard DC workflows but fails silently on custom workflow installations without any override mechanism

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the minimum (and optionally maximum) version of `pycontribs/jira` required for the `[jira-datacenter]` extra in the plan, e.g. `jira>=3.5,<4`.
evidence: 'gated behind a [jira-datacenter] extra and imported lazily'
'its JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…) surface covers DC-vs-Cloud divergence behind one client object'
No version pin or minimum version stated for pycontribs/jira anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The `[jira-datacenter]` optional extra's dependency on `pycontribs/jira` does not specify a minimum version or version range. The `pycontribs/jira` library's API surface and DC-vs-Cloud auth handling have changed across major versions, and the plan relies on `JIRA(server=…, token_auth=…)` being available.
findings.location: Approach §4 — 'DC transport builds on the maintained pycontribs/jira library'
scenarios: Executor pins `jira>=3.0` and the `token_auth` kwarg behavior differs from `jira==2.x` where it was introduced; integration tests break against older corporate Python environments.
A future `jira` 4.x breaking change silently ships into rebar's extra because the upper bound is unspecified.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `jira>=3.5,<4` (or the actual tested minimum) to the extra specification in Approach §4 and in the `pyproject.toml` scope bullet.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Merge the two operator-attested Dockerized Jira AC items into one, preserving all unique requirements: bidirectional verification, at least one inbound + one outbound change, zero unhandled exceptions, and reconcile log attached as a comment on the assembly story.
evidence: '[operator-attested] a full reconcile pass runs green against the Dockerized Jira with reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter", output attached as a comment on the assembly story'

'[operator-attested] rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira SDK instance at localhost:2990, selected by reconciler.backend = "jira-datacenter" … at least one issue created in DC appears in the local store after an inbound pass, and one local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass, with zero unhandled exceptions in the reconcile log'
findings.finding: Two operator-attested AC items substantially overlap: the first requires 'a full reconcile pass runs green against the Dockerized Jira … output attached as a comment on the assembly story'; the second requires 'rebar reconciles bidirectionally against the Dockerized Jira SDK instance at localhost:2990 … at least one issue created … one local edit … zero unhandled exceptions.' The second subsumes the first except for the 'output attached' artifact requirement, creating a near-duplicate that risks double-counting or confusing the verifier.
findings.location: AC items 2 and 6 (the two [operator-attested] Dockerized Jira criteria)
scenarios: Reviewer marks one criterion Done without the other; or the two criteria are assigned to different child stories, each doing half the verification work.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the method signatures (name, parameters, return type) for `RichTextCodec` and `UserIdentityModel` in the plan, or point to an interface stub committed as part of the shared-layer story.
evidence: 'a RichTextCodec (ADF for Cloud, wiki/plain text for DC) and a UserIdentityModel (accountId for Cloud, name for DC). Cloud is parameterized by its existing behavior; DC is a different configuration, not a fork.'
No method names, parameter types, or return types are specified for either contract object anywhere in the plan.
AC: 'the rich-text codec, and the user-identity model each have exactly one implementation reachable by both backends' — verifies existence, not interface correctness.
findings.finding: The `RichTextCodec` and `UserIdentityModel` contracts are introduced as new shared abstractions central to the seam design, but their method signatures, return types, and required interface surface are never specified. An executor implementing `adapters/jira_family/` and wiring both the Cloud and DC backends to them must invent these interfaces, which is a non-trivial design decision the plan defers to the implementor.
findings.location: Approach §3 — 'Pin the two real axes of variation as contracts'
scenarios: An executor writes a `RichTextCodec` with `encode(body: str) -> str`; a second executor writes DC transport assuming `render(text: str, format: Literal['wiki','plain']) -> str`; the seam breaks at integration.
The Cloud wiring of `RichTextCodec` is ambiguous: does it wrap the existing ADF encoder unchanged, or is a new adapter object introduced?
findings.suggested_fix: Add a subsection under Approach §3 listing at minimum: `RichTextCodec.encode_body(text: str) -> Any` (or equivalent), `UserIdentityModel.resolve(display_name: str) -> dict` (or equivalent), and state which module in `adapters/jira_family/` will define the abstract base or Protocol.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace 'DC EOL horizon' in the ADR AC with the specific fact to record (e.g., 'the 30 March 2026 trial-license cutoff and rebar's policy for DC support if Atlassian announces a DC sunset date').

The plan body mentions 'Atlassian stopped issuing DC trial licenses on 30 March 2026' but does not connect this to a 'DC EOL horizon' or state what rebar's policy is if/when Atlassian EOLs DC proper.
Atlassian's DC maintenance end dates vary by product version and have not been announced as a single EOL date.
findings.finding: The AC 'an ADR records the Jira-family sub-seam, the shared jira provenance identity, and the DC EOL horizon' uses the phrase 'DC EOL horizon' without defining what fact or date that refers to. Atlassian Data Center is not end-of-life; only trial licenses stopped on 30 March 2026. An executor writing the ADR cannot determine what commitment or date to record.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'an ADR records the Jira-family sub-seam...'
scenarios: Executor records the trial-license cutoff date (30 March 2026) as the 'EOL horizon'; reviewer rejects because DC software itself is supported until a different date.
ADR is written without this section because the executor cannot determine what to write; the AC is incorrectly marked done.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify the J2 behavior-preservation claim: either (a) state explicitly which caller's `deleted` key behavior the single unified dict will adopt (even if tentatively, pending `fe15`), or (b) reword J2's mandate to 'preserve Cloud Backend port behavior; ACLI-transport behavior is pinned by `fe15` before J2 lands'.
evidence: 'J2 unifies the maps preserving each caller's current observable behavior'
'the outbound_fields status map carries a deleted: Done entry the jira_fields copy lacks'
'the deleted-key drift is a behavior question (one of the two current behaviors is wrong), so it is NOT resolved inside J2's behavior-preserving move'
